# Application screenshot ownership

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. [The independent fixture](released-application-screenshots.json), SHA-256 `0c61a1e0e099b844c2e9b58cce24b313e1c48a8f94e3bf47c759755622b74dab`, records seventeen actual application workflows and 79 GTK/store/clipboard/editor states, plus terminal ownership and HTTP requests. The temporary observer activates the unchanged released application and invokes its actual actions, widgets and shutdown; imported reference modules are checked byte-for-byte against the pinned commit. It lives only in ignored `tmp/`. Native checks consume the frozen observations without an interpreter.

The native comparison constructs the actual `ApplicationDesktop`, capture services/controller/session, compatible providers, shared History/screenshot stores and GTK screenshot shelf. Separate native processes supply synthetic PCM, the external `omarchy screenshot region save` boundary and an editor that saves real managed PNG files. The editor and picker peers import no Mluva implementation. Actual GIO file-monitor events refresh the displayed previews. HTTP traffic stays on private loopback; requests compare complete audio/image bytes and image ordering. Tests inspect public widgets and externally visible process/file/store results, with no production test hooks.

The workflows cover a saved owner frozen before switching to a different conversation; actual editor saves and duplicate-open prevention; close-before-delete, including an editor that ignores TERM; recording and continuation images; silent and failed recordings with images; cancellation and shutdown with attached images or pending selection; shutdown during processing; Incognito cancellation; Scratchpad/no-owner restrictions; invalid selection, including while Stop waits; and deletion of the frozen owner before selection returns. The released application leaves external editors running when Mluva closes, while cancelling their file monitors. Explicit image deletion first terminates and reaps the editor, then deletes its file. The synthetic editor saves again on TERM, so reversing that order leaves a detectable resurrected PNG.

Stop finalizes audio and streaming/batch-preview recognition before waiting for selection to attach or be discarded. Only then does it freeze image input for the remaining workflow. One case deliberately fails the preview request, holds the subsequent batch fallback request, and edits the attached file while processing. The saved image changes to green while the actual rewrite request retains the earlier red PNG. The continuation case sends the existing blue image followed by the newly selected red image. Silent/failed captures create the same screenshot-owning History entries as the release. The component's real 180-second picker deadline is recorded separately in [process-owner evidence](../../../mluva-workflows/tests/fixtures/screenshot-capture-evidence.md); this application check does not repeat that three-minute test.

Two additional native faults exercise lifecycle protection. A real SQLite trigger rejects the screenshot-only History write: selected pixels remain owned by the pending capture, survive application exit, and recover through the real startup service once the database accepts writes again. This case also exercises the explicit installed-editor path rather than PATH fallback. A delayed audio process reproduced a race in which a picker result opened an editor after Cancel while recorder cleanup was still pending. The application now rejects that result and new screenshot requests during cancellation. The final check verifies no image, editor, upload or History entry is created by the late result. These are native fault protections, not claims of identical released behavior under those faults.

The first native comparison failed because the screenshot action was still an external placeholder. After wiring, all seventeen released workflows match. The delayed-cancellation check then failed before the ownership guard was added and passes after it. Every application shutdown additionally verifies that its actual picker PID and temporary screenshot directories are gone. The selected editor is intentionally left running when required by the released contract and is stopped by the test only after that behavior is observed. Generated entry/image/capture identities are mapped consistently within each workflow. Narration offsets are checked as finite values in `[0, 8)` and represented as `sampled`; exact image data, displayed captions, GTK-encoded preview pixels and HTTP image order are retained. Toolkit versions are pinned by the fixture. This is not a complete-window pixel comparison or a timing/performance claim.

The canonical `make linux-screenshot-test` now prepares the external peers and private environment automatically, after running the [actual app-launched narrated editor comparison](application-images-evidence.md). For this lifecycle owner alone, use `bash linux/tests/run_application_smoke.sh screenshots`. The test checks isolation before creating any synthetic executable. The isolated runner provides DISPLAY, HOME/XDG, accessibility/session buses, network/PID/mount namespaces and masked devices; no host pixels/input/clipboard, microphone, credentials or user content are used. The equivalent low-level invocation requires `MLUVA_DISABLE_GLOBAL_SHORTCUT=1`, `TZ=UTC`, `MLUVA_SCREENSHOT_FIXTURE_ROOT=$OFFSCREEN_SESSION_ROOT/application-screenshot-case`, and `$MLUVA_SCREENSHOT_FIXTURE_ROOT/tools` first in PATH:

```sh
cargo build --locked -p mluva-audio --bin audio-fixture-peer --bin mluva-audio-cleanup
cargo build --locked -p mluva-workflows --bin screenshot-picker-fixture-peer
cargo build --locked -p mluva-gtk --example screenshot_editor_peer
# Within the guarded private session, with the environment described above:
cargo test --locked -p mluva-gtk --test application_screenshots -- \
  --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

The affected assembled application, capture factory, capture lifecycle, Live, application shortcuts, History and Command/Notes comparisons also pass: eight/56, six/eight, 46/218, 26/122, eight/34, fifteen/59 and nineteen/71 released workflows/states respectively, with their existing native faults. Whole-workspace ordinary checks and strict all-target Clippy remain separate gates. Development peers must be excluded from distribution. The separate [native narration comparison](../../../mluva-workflows/tests/fixtures/narration-evidence.md) now exercises the actual Tensaku canvas with the Rust helper. Executable/bootstrap, real Omarchy region selection on private Wayland, physical F10, complete joined editor/Live/image and screenshot deletion/retention paths, supported platforms, package/Python removal and performance acceptance remain required. All complete-workflow parity rows remain Pending; the installed app/widget remain verified 1.6.0.
